title: Wearable Core Body Temperature Monitoring for Early Detection of Cytokine Release Syndrome in Outpatients Receiving CAR T-Cell Therapy
official: A Randomized Controlled Trial of a Wearable Core Body Temperature Sensor Versus Standard Temperature Monitoring for Early Detection of Cytokine Release Syndrome in Patients Undergoing CAR T-Cell Therapy in an Outpatient Setting
summary: The purpose of this research study is to see if a wearable temperature monitoring patch can detect cytokine release syndrome earlier than traditional oral temperature monitoring.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Patients:

1. Ability to understand and willingness to sign an IRB-approved informed consent
2. Age ≥ 18 years at the time of consent
3. Scheduled to undergo CAR-T therapy in the outpatient setting at AHWFBCCC
4. Ability to read and understand the English and/or Spanish language
5. As determined by the enrolling investigator, ability of the participant to understand and comply with study procedures for the entire length of the study
6. Access to a mobile device for the duration of the trial

Provider/Staff:

Provider/staff participants must meet all of the following inclusion criteria to participate in the study:

1. Verbally agree to participate
2. Hospital at Home outpatient provider/advanced practice provider/nurse of at least one patient participant enrolled on Arm A who completed 14 days of temperature monitoring

Exclusion Criteria:

Patients:

1. Planned prophylactic tocilizumab for mitigation of CRS as documented in the clinical trials pathway submission
2. History of silicone allergy
3. History of Medical Adhesive-Related Skin Injury (MARSI)
4. Known skin condition that might preclude safe application of the patch, in the opinion of the enrolling investigator

Provider/Staff:

None
